question: Who is the most famous Midwestern athlete of all time?

answers:
Determining the "most famous" athlete of all time from the Midwest is subjective and may vary based on personal opinions and the criteria used for fame. However, one notable Midwestern athlete is Michael Jordan, the basketball legend from Chicago. His talent was evident from his very first NBA season. Larry Bird famously said he had "never seen anyone like him," describing Jordan as "one of a kind" and the best player he had ever seen. In terms of athleticism, Jordan draws comparisons to Wayne Gretzky.
During Jordan's first game at Madison Square Garden against the New York Knicks, he received a prolonged standing ovation, a rare honor for an opposing player. Furthermore, after Jordan scored a playoff record 63 points against the Boston Celtics on April 20, 1986, Bird remarked that he was "God disguised as Michael Jordan."

Is there a radio station that regularly broadcasts their games?

Yes, the St. Louis Cardinals Radio Network broadcasts St. Louis Cardinals baseball games. The network comprises 111 stations: 52 AM and 59 FM, along with six FM translators across nine states. Here are some of the stations:
- WQKZ / 98.5 FM: Ferdinand
- WQTY / 93.3 FM: Linton (Vincennes/Terre Haute area)
- KWON / 1400 AM: Bartlesville

- KGFF / 1450 AM: Shawnee
- WMFS-FM / 92.9 FM: Bartlett
- WKFN / 540 AM: Clarksville
- WTRO / 1450 AM: Dyersburg
- WMUF / 104.7 FM: Henry (Paris area)
- WZLT / 99.3 FM: Lexington

- Kansas City: Chiefs (NFL), Royals (MLB), Sporting KC (MLS)
- Milwaukee: Brewers (MLB), Bucks (NBA)
- Minneapolis-Saint Paul: Vikings (NFL), Twins (MLB), Timberwolves (NBA), Wild (NHL), United FC (MLS)
- St. Louis: Cardinals (MLB), Blues (NHL)

The protagonist of the novel is Raymond Davis Garraty , a 16 - year - old boy from the town of Pownal in Androscoggin County , Maine . Early on , he falls in with several other boys -- including Peter McVries , Arthur Baker , Hank Olson , Collie Parker , Pearson , Harkness , and Abraham -- who refer to themselves as `` The Musketeers '' .
